## Overview
 Happi House opened February 29, 1976 in San Jose's historic Japantown.   It was founded by Mr. Joe Ikeda, Dr. Carlo Besio and Mr. Richard Tanaka, three partners who believed quick service and family restaurant menus had become predictably boring. 

## Name and Origin
 The restaurant was named "Happi House" after the traditional Japanese garment, the Happi Coat, which is a lightweight cotton jacket worn during festivals and celebrations.   Inspired by the popular foods of Japantown's famous Obon Festival, the partners agreed that their restaurant would always prepare fresh and delicious Asian style meals. 

## Philosophy and Food
 The founding partners agreed that meals would be cooked to order and be offered at a family-friendly price, and together with time-honored family recipes and an innovative cooking system, Happi House was the first restaurant of its kind.   The menu features options like teriyaki plates, rice bowls, noodles, and salads, offering convenient and flavorful meals for dine-in, takeout, and catering. 

## Current Status
 Happi House has been serving fresh and fast food including tempura for over 40 years in the San Francisco Bay Area.  The restaurant operates as a chain with multiple locations in the Bay Area.
